Petition under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act, 1988 for grant of compensation AWARD 1.

By way of present judgment/award, I shall dispose of the DAR filed by the investigating agency which has been converted into a claim petition under section 166(4) of M. V. Act 1988 for grant of compensation to the petitioners.

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim petition as averred are that on 17.06.2019 at about 10:15 AM, the petitioner/injured was crossing the road near G-3 Block, Mother Dairy towards Sector - 17, Mother Dairy, Rohini, Delhi when the offending vehicle bearing no.
DL11-SC-0213 i.e. a black colour Splendor motorcycle which was being driven by its driver (respondent no. 1 herein) at a very high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from the Bawana side and hit him with great force due to which he fell down on the road and he sustained grievous injuries in his left leg.
He was immediately taken to Dr. BSA Hospital, Rohini, Delhi.

A case under section 279/338 IPC & 3/181 M.V. Act was registered vide FIR No. 409/19 at PS. K.N.K. Marg with regard to the MACP No. 156/20; FIR No. 409/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 14.02.2024 accident in question.
The offending vehicle is claimed to be owned by respondent no. 2/registered owner namely Sh. Sudhir.
According to DAR, the offending vehicle was found to be uninsured at the time of accident.

3. Although, the respondent no. 1 & 2 i.e. driver and registered owner put their appearance before this Tribunal on 27.02.2020 i.e. on the date of filing of DAR but they failed to file their written statement despite grant of sufficient time and opportunities.
Ultimately, their defence was struck off vide order dated 25.02.2021.
4. In support of his claim, the petitioner has examined only one witness i.e. himself as PW1 and his evidence was closed vide order dated 24.05.2023.
5. Ld.
Counsel for petitioner/injured was heard at length and the record was perused carefully.
6. For the purpose of determination of award in the present case, the testimony of PW1 Sh. Kuldeep Singh i.e. injured himself is relevant.

PW1 has deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex.
PW1/A) on the similar averments as made in DAR.

He has relied upon the following documents:-
S.No. Description of documents Remarks 1. Copy of his Aadhaar Card Ex PW1/1 2. Copy of his Driving Licence Ex. PW1/2  MACP No. 156/20; FIR No. 409/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg  Kuldeep Singh vs Rohit Kumar on 14 February, 2024

7.
The ocular testimony of aforesaid witness  unchallanged and uncontroverted from the side of respondents, who preferred not to contest the petition and stayed away from the proceedings.
Thus, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of petitioner, made on oath.
8. Moreover, the ocular testimony of petitioner is also corroborated by documentary evidence brought on record.
FIR No. 409/19 was registered at PS. K.N.K. Marg with regard to accident in question.

Copy of said FIR would show that same was registered on the statement of petitioner himself wherein he stated about the same sequence of events which led to the accident in question,
as narrated by him as PW1 during his testimony recorded in this case.

The very fact that respondent no. 1 namely Sh. Rohit Kumar was charge-sheeted (which is part of DAR) by the police for offences punishable u/s. 279/338 IPC & 3/181 M.V. Act would further show that Investigating Agency also concluded after completion of the investigation that said accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Thus, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and / or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of the petitioner.
MACP No. 156/20; FIR No. 409/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 14.02.2024 9.
Not only this, the respondent no. 1 was a material witness, who could have thrown light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he preferred not to enter into witness box, during the course of inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

10. Apart from above, copy of MLC (Ex. PW1/3) of injured prepared at Dr. BSA Hospital, Delhi shows that he had been removed to said hospital on 17.06.2019 at about 10:43 AM with alleged history of Road Traffic Accident (RTA) i.e on the date of accident, immediately after the accident.
On his local examination, he was found to have sustained multiple injuries as mentioned therein.
The said injuries are consistent with the injuries which are sustained in motor vehicular accident.
Again, there is no challenge to the said document from the side of respondents.

11. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that he had sustained grievous injuries in road accident which took place on 17.06.2019 at about 10:15 AM, near G-3 Block, Mother Dairy towards Sector - 17, Mother Dairy, Rohini, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1.

3 12.
Now, the question arises as to how much amount of compensation which is just and fair, should be awarded in favour of the petitioner.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be niggardly.
MEDICAL EXPENSES 13.
In his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, PW1 Sh. Kuldeep Singh (injured himself) has deposed that after the accident, he was removed to BSA Hospital, Rohini, Delhi.
He further deposed that he had sustained grievous injuries i.e. fracture tibia, due to accident in question.
He further deposed that he had incurred a sum of Rs. 50,000/- on his medical treatment.

The respondents no.
1 & 2 did not cross-
examine the said witness.
14. It is relevant to note that the petitioner has failed to file any of his medical bills.
It may be noted here that petitioner had received treatment from the government hospital.
Since, there is no medical bills filed/relied upon by the petitioner, no amount is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
MACP No. 156/20; FIR No. 409/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 14.02.2024 LOSS OF INCOME 15.
The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that he was working as an Auto Driver and earning Rs. 20,000/- per month at the time of accident.
He further deposed that due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident, he remained bed-ridden for long period and as such, suffered loss of income.
He further deposed that he had suffered financial loss due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident in question.
His testimony remained unrebutted and unchallenged on this aspect.

16. Apart from the aforesaid document i.e. MLC (Ex. PW1/3 colly), the petitioner has failed to file any other medical treatment record in order to show the exact period upto which he had received the medical treatment.
Nevertheless, it can not be overlooked that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries i.e. fracture tibia.
It is also relevant to note here that petitioner had also sustained 20% permanent disability in relation to left lower limb.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner as well as the permanent disability suffered by him, it is presumed that he would not have been able to work at all atleast for a period of 3 months or so.

17. Apart from the bald statement made by PW1 Sh. Kuldeep Singh that he was working as Driver and earning Rs. 20,000/-per month at the time of accident, no definite evidence whatsoever has been brought on record to prove his monthly income at the time of accident in question.

However,
the MACP No. 156/20; FIR No. 409/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 14.02.2024 petitioner has filed copy of his graduation certificate Ex. PW1/5.

In the absence of any such document with regard to working and earning of petitioner/injured, I am of the view that loss of income of the petitioner has to be assessed while taking the income of a graduate person under Minimum Wages Act applicable during the period in question The minimum wages of a graduate person were Rs. 19,060/- per month as on the date of accident which is 17.06.2019.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 57,180/- (Rs. 19,060/- x 3) is awarded in favour of petitioner under this head.

He might have also consumed heavy dose of anti-biotic etc. and also might have remained without movements of his body for a considerable period of time.

In order to ascertain the pain and sufferings compensation, I am guided by the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No.709/02, date of decision: 2.2.2007,

sentences.text: However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a)Nature of injury.
(b)Body part affected.
(c)Duration of the treatment."
19.

As already considered, the petitioner required treatment for a period of about three months from the date of accident and remained incapacitated to resume his work of earnings for at least a period of three months owing to grievous injuries suffered in the road traffic accident.
Thus, he would have undergone great physical sufferings, inconvenience and mental trauma on account of the accident in question.
Keeping in view the nature of injuries, duration of treatment and permanent disability suffered by him, a sum of Rs. 60,000/- is considered reasonable towards pain & sufferings.
LOSS OF GENERAL AMENITIES & ENJOYMENT OF LIFE 20.
As already mentioned above, there is sufficient evidence on record to establish that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.
Apart from this, the petitioner is also shown to have sustained permanent disability to the extent of 20% in relation to his left lower limb.
Thus, he would not be able to enjoy general amenities of life after the accident in question and his quality of life has been definitely affected.

In view of the nature of injuries including permanent disability suffered by him MACP No. 156/20; FIR No. 409/19; PS. K.N.K. Marg DOD: 14.02.2024 and his continued treatment for a considerable period, I award a notional sum of Rs. 50,000/-

Thus, he would have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred considerable amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular check up & follow up during the period of his medical treatment.
He would have been definitely helped by some person either outsider or from his family, to perform his daily activities as also while visiting the hospital during the course of his medical treatment.

In these facts and circumstances, I hereby award a notional sum of Rs. 10,000/-
